title: Measuring a mountain nobody had climbed

back: In 1852 Radhanath Sikdar is credited with working out, from measured angles, that Peak XV (Everest) was the highest known.

title: Angle of elevation and angle of depression
back: Both are measured from the horizontal. The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the ground.

title: Height from distance and angle
back: Use tan when the question gives a height and a distance along the ground.

title: A rope, ladder or kite string
back: The slant length is the hypotenuse: sin for the height, cos for the foot distance.

title: Sun's elevation from a shadow
back: Shadow = height: 45°. Shadow = √3 × height: 30°. Height = √3 × shadow: 60°.

title: Two points on the same side
back: Two triangles share the height. Write $h=x\tan60^\circ$ and $h=(x+40)\tan30^\circ$, then solve: $h=20\sqrt3$ m.

title: Looking up and down from one point
back: Draw the horizontal through the observer. Lower part = building height; upper part from tan 60°. Add the two.

title: Two objects seen from a tower
back: The nearer object always has the larger angle.

title: Observer of height 1.5 m
back: The triangle starts at eye level. Forgetting this loses the last mark.

title: Every heights-and-distances answer
back: The labelled figure carries a mark. Keep √3 as a surd until the last line.
